newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CHANG, KORDA WIN SEMIFINALS IN WASHINGTON TENNIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG, KORDA WIN SEMIFINALS IN WASHINGTON TENNIS.

text.p: Michael Chang started off
strongly, romping to a 6-2 victory in the first set, but he
sputtered in the second before beating Brett Steven 7-4 in the
tiebreaker in the semifinals at the $675,000 Legg Mason Tennis
Classic on Saturday.
In the other match, second-seed Petr Korda of the Czech
Republic) beat David Wheaton 6-2 6-3.
Top-seed Chang was down 1-4 to a revitalised 11th seeded
Steven in the second set. But Chang rallied to run off three
games to tie the set and made Steven work hard to hold
serrvice and gain a tie-breaker.
Chang ran to a 3-0 lead and held his service until
finishing the match off with an overhead smash.
"Things have continued to get better for me this week and
maybe I have those tough early matches to thank for it. Being
poushed was good for me. I had to hit a lot of balls and
that's always good when you're making the transition to
hardcourts (from grass)."
Korda breezed past Wheaton, who had a hip lock up on him
and spent most of the match "feeling like my feet were in
cement."
Korda suffered from the effects of the heat in the earlier
rounds and said his match against Wheaton "would have been a
struggle if this had turned into a long match. I went in quite
weak."
